skills.trigger: When evaluating a mediastinal mass or tracheal abnormality on CT to determine its vertical extent and relationship to adjacent structures.
steps: Identify the trachea on axial slices by locating the air-filled structure anterior to the esophagus and posterior to the great vessels.

Determine the vertical level of the finding by correlating axial slices with coronal/sagittal reconstructions; distinguish the upper third (suprasternal notch to thoracic inlet) from the middle/lower thirds based on proximity to the aortic arch and carina.
Assess tracheal deviation by comparing the position of the tracheal air column relative to the midline spine and sternum; note if deviation is towards or away from the mass.

skills.trigger: When correlating imaging findings of an upper mediastinal/tracheal mass with clinical symptoms of dysphonia (hoarseness).
steps: Confirm the mass is located in the upper mediastinum or superior thoracic aperture where the recurrent laryngeal nerves course.
Evaluate for direct invasion or compression of the trachea and paratracheal regions, which are anatomical pathways for the recurrent laryngeal nerves.

Distinguish this mechanism from intrinsic tracheal lesions (which typically cause stridor/obstruction) or lower mediastinal masses (which are less likely to affect vocal cord innervation), supporting dysphonia as a symptom of nerve involvement rather than primary airway obstruction.
